title: 2.2 Pulse Crops Production and Management
description: Pulses: nitrogen fixation, cultivation and management

questions.question: What are pulses?
options: Seeds of legume crops that are grown mainly for their edible seeds
Grains of grass crops that are grown mainly for their edible seeds
Stems of cereal crops that are used as livestock feed
Roots of tuber crops that are grown below the ground
questions.correctAnswer: Seeds of legume crops that are grown mainly for their edible seeds

questions.question: In what two forms are pulses consumed?
options: As dry seeds rich in protein and as immature pods used as vegetables
As dry seeds rich in fat and as mature pods used as fuel
As fresh green leaves and as roasted seeds
As boiled seeds and as extracted oil
questions.correctAnswer: As dry seeds rich in protein and as immature pods used as vegetables

questions.question: Besides being used as human food, pulses also serve as what?
options: A source of animal feed
A source of cooking oil
A source of building timber
A source of industrial starch
questions.correctAnswer: A source of animal feed

questions.question: Pulse crops are classified as which type of plants?
options: Dicots
Monocots
Grasses
Tuberous plants
questions.correctAnswer: Dicots

questions.question: Many pulse crops assist with which soil related process?
options: Nitrogen fixation
Salinity reduction
Erosion control by terracing
Flood water harvesting
questions.correctAnswer: Nitrogen fixation

questions.question: Through which structure do pulse plants fix atmospheric nitrogen into the soil?
options: Root nodules
Leaf hairs
Seed coats
Flower petals
questions.correctAnswer: Root nodules

questions.question: What happens to the nitrogen that pulse crops fix from the atmosphere?
options: It becomes available in the soil for subsequent crops
It is lost from the soil through evaporation
It is stored only in the stems of the pulse plants
It is transferred to the irrigation water
questions.correctAnswer: It becomes available in the soil for subsequent crops

questions.question: Why can pulses be used in crop rotations to improve soil fertility?
options: They fix atmospheric nitrogen and leave it in the soil for later crops
They raise the soil temperature by several degrees
They prevent the soil from losing all of its moisture
They turn clay soils into sandy soils
questions.correctAnswer: They fix atmospheric nitrogen and leave it in the soil for later crops

questions.question: With which type of crop are pulses commonly grown in mixed cropping?
options: Cereals
Root crops
Fibre crops
Tree crops
questions.correctAnswer: Cereals

questions.question: What is the main purpose of growing pulses together with cereals?
options: To improve the yield of the cereal crop
To reduce the taste of the cereal grain
To shorten the growing period of the cereal
To keep the field free of livestock
questions.correctAnswer: To improve the yield of the cereal crop

questions.question: In Ethiopia, pulses are mostly produced in which way regarding mineral fertilizer?
options: Without mineral fertilizer application
With heavy mineral fertilizer application
With mineral fertilizer applied only at flowering
With mineral fertilizer applied by aerial spraying
questions.correctAnswer: Without mineral fertilizer application

questions.question: Which organic fertilizer is sometimes used in pulse production in Ethiopia?
options: Animal manure
Green alga slurry
Wood ash from forest fires
Rock phosphate powder
questions.correctAnswer: Animal manure

questions.question: How does soil cultivation for pulses generally compare with soil cultivation for cereals?
options: It is generally minimal
It is repeated about five times
It is always carried out by machines
It is carried out only after harvesting
questions.correctAnswer: It is generally minimal

questions.question: What are the two forms of minimal soil cultivation described for pulses?
options: The soil is cultivated once, or direct planting takes place with no soil cultivation
The soil is cultivated once, or it is cultivated ten times
The soil is cultivated twice, or it is irrigated twice
The soil is never cultivated and never planted
questions.correctAnswer: The soil is cultivated once, or direct planting takes place with no soil cultivation

questions.question: What does direct planting mean in pulse production?
options: Planting takes place with no soil cultivation
Planting takes place twice in one season
Planting takes place only after the first rain
Planting takes place using a planting machine
questions.correctAnswer: Planting takes place with no soil cultivation

questions.question: Which problem, together with minimal cultivation, has resulted in low pulse yields in Ethiopia?
options: Poor weed control in grain legumes
Excessive use of animal manure
Very deep ploughing of the soil
Use of improved crop varieties
questions.correctAnswer: Poor weed control in grain legumes

questions.question: What is the likely result of poor weed control in grain legume fields?
options: Low yields
High yields
Faster seed maturity
Better nitrogen fixation
questions.correctAnswer: Low yields

questions.question: Which are the three major pulse crops in Ethiopia?
options: Faba bean, field pea and haricot bean
Teff, maize and sorghum
Wheat, barley and teff
Faba bean, lentil and soybean
questions.correctAnswer: Faba bean, field pea and haricot bean

questions.question: How many major pulse crops are listed for Ethiopia in this unit?
options: Three
Two
Four
Five
questions.correctAnswer: Three

questions.question: Which group of crops do faba bean, field pea and haricot bean belong to?
options: Pulses (legumes)
Cereals
Root and tuber crops
Fibre crops
questions.correctAnswer: Pulses (legumes)

questions.question: Into which two major groups are field crops classified?
options: Cereals and pulses (legumes)
Cereals and root crops
Pulses and oil crops
Vegetables and fruits
questions.correctAnswer: Cereals and pulses (legumes)

questions.question: Cereal crops are monocots, meaning their seeds have how many cotyledons?
options: A single cotyledon
Two cotyledons
Three cotyledons
No cotyledon
questions.correctAnswer: A single cotyledon

questions.question: What is meant by annual field crops?
options: Crops that complete a life cycle in a single season
Crops that live for many years
Crops that are harvested every two years
Crops that grow only in the dry season
questions.correctAnswer: Crops that complete a life cycle in a single season

questions.question: A farmer rotates a cereal with faba bean. What benefit does the faba bean give to the cereal?
options: It improves soil fertility through nitrogen fixation
It supplies the cereal with extra irrigation
It protects the cereal seed from storage weevils
It shortens the maturity period of the cereal
questions.correctAnswer: It improves soil fertility through nitrogen fixation

questions.question: A farmer grows haricot bean together with maize in the same field. What is the expected result?
options: The yield of the maize crop is improved
The maize crop is completely destroyed
The haricot bean stops fixing nitrogen
Both crops mature within one week
questions.correctAnswer: The yield of the maize crop is improved

questions.question: How does the number of cultivations for teff compare with that for pulses?
options: Teff soil is cultivated 4 or 5 times while pulse soil cultivation is minimal
Teff soil is cultivated once while pulse soil is cultivated 5 times
Both crops require exactly the same number of cultivations
Teff is direct planted while pulses are cultivated five times
questions.correctAnswer: Teff soil is cultivated 4 or 5 times while pulse soil cultivation is minimal

questions.question: What effect does growing pulses have on the nitrogen status of a field?
options: It increases the nitrogen available in the soil for later crops
It removes all nitrogen from the soil
It prevents nitrogen from entering the soil
It changes nitrogen into a mineral nutrient unavailable to plants
questions.correctAnswer: It increases the nitrogen available in the soil for later crops

questions.question: Which practice in pulse production would the handout identify as needing improvement to raise yields?
options: Weed control in grain legumes
The number of seed colours
The taste of the seeds
The colour of the crop residues
questions.correctAnswer: Weed control in grain legumes
